(a) Section 3313.—Section 3313 is amended—
        (1) by striking “higher education” each place it appears and inserting “higher learning”; and 
        (2) in clause (iii) of subparagraph (A) of subsection (e)(2), as redesignated by section 103(a)(2) of this Act, by adding a period at the end.  
    (b) Section 3319.—Section 3319(b)(2) is amended by striking “to section (k)” and inserting “to subsection (j)”. 
    (c) Section 3323.—Section 3323(a) is amended by striking “section 3034(a)(1)” and inserting “sections 3034(a)(1) and 3680(c)”.

fable.w: This section makes only technical and conforming amendments to statutory text (word substitutions, punctuation, and cross-reference corrections). No outside party is consulted, heard, or given any right to challenge a federal decision; there is no tempting participation language at all.

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to other statutory provisions, such as changing terminology ('higher education' to 'higher learning') and correcting cross-references. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. The text is purely legislative housekeeping.

opus.w: This section only makes technical edits: it swaps "higher education" for "higher learning," adds a period, and fixes cross-references in sections 3313, 3319 and 3323. Nothing in it brings anyone outside the federal government into a federal decision. There is no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue. The only possible pull toward "Yes" is that the cross-referenced sections might involve outside parties, but that text isn't in front of us and this section creates no process of its own.

qwen_chat.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to other sections of the statute, such as changing terminology from 'higher education' to 'higher learning' and correcting punctuation or cross-references. It does not create any new requirement for the federal government to consult with or coordinate with non-federal entities, nor does it establish advisory bodies, public comment periods, or rights to sue. Therefore, it does not involve participation as defined.
qwen_chat.s: (a) Section 3313.—Section 3313 is amended— (1) by striking “higher education” each place it appears and inserting “higher learning”; and (2) in clause (iii) of subparagraph (A) of subsection (e)(2), as redesignated by section 103(a)(2) of this Act, by adding a period at the end.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because these amendments change the text of other statutes, they implicitly affect participation processes defined elsewhere. However, this specific section only contains technical corrections (changing "higher education" to "higher learning", fixing punctuation, and updating cross-references). It does not itself establish, require, or describe any process of consultation, coordination, or involvement with non-federal parties.
